stances.summary: Suggests Chinese regulators prioritize property market recovery
stances.quote: Not sure, but perhaps they were worried that tighter rules might slow down a recovery in the property market. Nearly all of their recent property-related policies have been in the direction of easing.

stances.summary: Characterizes property market as revealing deeper economic disparities
stances.quote:
Very interesting Caixin article on China's K-shaped property market, with a sliver of premium properties in top-tier cities seeming to recover strongly while everything else continues to flounder. As always, the property market is a mirror of the economy.
www.caixinglobal.com/202

stances.summary: Notes China's economic challenges require foreign consumer stimulus
stances.quote:
Wow. According to SCMP, "Attracting foreign consumers has become a key strategy for China to stimulate its slowing economy. As the country’s gateway city, Shanghai holds natural advantages in this arena, which are reflected in its officials’ ambitions."

stances.summary: Notes tightening job safety net for graduates signals deteriorating labor market
stances.quote:
Good, but worrying, Caixin article: "A bruising labor market is driving record numbers of Chinese college graduates to low-paying grassroots community jobs, but local governments are increasingly closing the door on this once-reliable employment safety net."
www.caixinglobal.com/

stances.summary: Rebalancing from low consumption historically painful, unavoidable for China
stances.quote:
3/3
Unfortunately, this is typically how economies with extremely low consumptions shares have always ended up rebalancing their economies once they no longer have much scope for increasing investment or increasing debt.

stances.summary: Higher wages risk reducing total production rather than boosting consumption
stances.quote:
2/3
SCMP gets it exactly right. Higher wages are certainly a good way to rebalance, but with so many Chinese businesses struggling to make a profit, higher wages risk boosting the consumption share of GDP not by raising total wages but by reducing total production.

stances.summary: Minimum wage increases unlikely to significantly boost consumption or economy
stances.quote:
1/3
SCMP: "As more Chinese provinces raise minimum wages, economists say the increases could encourage lower-income workers to spend more, but were unlikely to significantly boost consumption or the broader economy, and could add to the cost burdens faced by smaller firms."
sc.mp

stances.summary: Trade imbalance adjustment is painful; key question is how burden distributed
stances.quote:
In my most recent piece for Foreign Affairs, I argue that we actually know quite a lot about how large trade imbalances eventually get resolved – and that the adjustment is almost always painful. The key question, then, is how it will be distributed.
www.foreignaffairs.com/united

stances.summary: IMF now embraces position it long resisted on trade imbalances
stances.quote:
3/e
Good news. Over the past year or two the IMF seems to have made an about-face and now fully embraces what it has long resisted.

stances.summary: Global incentive structure flawed; Thailand trapped in debt-wage-competitiveness bind
stances.quote:
10/10
This is a terrible global incentive structure. The only way Thailand can reduce household debt without slowing the economy either is to raise wages or to run surpluses, but it can't raise wages without making its manufacturers less competitive.
